BARCLAYS - YASH TAILOR 
 
Barclays visited our campus for the internship hiring process. The 
criteria kept by Barclays was CPI>6.5 and no active backlogs. Only 
CS and IT branches were allowed to sit for the interview process. 
Even DSYs were not allowed. 
 
Stage 1: The Online Test 
Around 60+ students sat for the online test. The test was conducted 
on Hackerearth platform and had 30 MCQs and 2 programming 
questions. The test was of 2.5 hrs.  
 
Type of the 30 MCQs are as follows: 
1) Programming languages: C,C++,Java, JavaScript and Python 
(A lot of regex questions) 
2) OOPS: C++ and Java 
3) Cloud (Azure) 
4) Servlets 
MCQs had no negative marking so that's the bonus point. Unlike 
Goldman Sachs :/ 
 
VIMP​ : For MCQ type questions make sure your fundamentals of 
OOP are strong and the concepts used in both C++ and Java, 
practise python questions, read a few points about cloud 
platforms(what all they offer, limits of all the features they provide, 
naming conventions, etc), Servlets are always asked, so make sure 
you know how to make requests and specify parameters in the 
same.  
 
Programming questions: 
 
1) Problem Statement​ : Given, a function f : C -> C, here C is 
a complex number, we have been given an array A[] such that 
for every A[i], f​A[i]​(x) = x. So, say an array contains 1,2 and 4, 
then f(x)=x, f²(x)=x and f⁴(x)=x. Now, consider a set G of 
which every element of satisfies the property that f​G(i)​(x) = x. 
Further, after determining G, we need to tell whether the 
complement of G, i.e. G’ is FINITE or INFINITE.

Type​: Number Theory 
Link​:​https://www.hackerearth.com/practice/math/number-the
ory/basic-number-theory-2/practice-problems/algorithm/is-it-f
inite-36fe70d5/ 
 
This was a pretty interesting question, I struggled till the end 
to figure this out but was happy to make it through.  
 
2) Problem Statement ​: Given two arrays we need to find the 
number of triplets whose relative order is the same in both the 
arrays. 
Type​: DP 
Link​:​https://www.hackerrank.com/challenges/count-triplets-1
/problem 
 
This was a fairly difficult question if we ignore the brute force 
approach. 
 
If you have solved ​at least one programming question​, your 
chances of getting selected increases. 
 
After the online test, 23 people were shortlisted for the interview 
round. 
 
Round 2: Interview Round (Technical + HR) 
 
The interview started with a typical “tell me about yourself, 
background and description of the projects” . I explained every 
project​ in the following way: 
1) Motivation behind the project 
2) Tech stack used 
3) Few important points if any. (For example, I have a project 
which was done under Mumbai Vikas Samiti, an NGO and told 
the entire backstory of it too) 
It went for around 15–20 mins.

Then he started asking me ​questions on OOPS 
 
1) What is inheritance? 
2) What is the difference between multiple and multilevel 
inheritance? 
3) What are the restrictions of Inheritance? 
4) Difference between private and protected access specifier 
(explained in both C++ and Java) 
5) What are the characteristics of OOP? 
6) Explain polymorphism 
7) What is superclass and subclass? 
 
Then he started asking me a bunch of ​HR questions​:  
1) Whether I like to work in a team or individually? 
Team. Talked about all the managerial work I did till that 
day, My Internship experience, group projects. 
2) What were the Challenges faced while working in a team and 
how did I mitigate them? 
My response: Talked about patience, taking appropriate 
decisions, mentioned about the problems which I faced 
during my Internship and how I managed them. 
3) Why Barclays?  
My response: To which I asked if I can answer why banks 
and then why Barclays. I did thorough research on 
Barclays, hence told them everything I knew about them, 
all their firsts in the UK, be it their sponsorship for people 
who were the first to reach Mount Everest summit in UK, 
connect, Barclaycard, first ATM machine, etc. I 
specifically added their values (RISES) 
4) He then asked me how can I contribute to the Stewardship? 
Go through their website, it has enough points :”) 
5) Any questions for him?  
I asked him three questions. Always prepare a set of 
questions to be asked out of which one should be related 
to their current affairs. It shows your interest towards 
them.

Finally out of 23 students, 4 were selected and I was one of them. 
PS. After a month or so, they sent a list of 6 more people kept in 
the waiting list. Miracles happen any time :) 
 
General Note:  
1) Stay super confident. 
2) Make sure know enough about the company(history + 
branches + products + domain) 
3) Barclays tip: Make sure you know DBMS and OOP well.  
4) Never give up :)
